transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hello, Doctor. Thank you so much for taking the time to see me. I hope I'm not wasting your time, I just... well, I wasn't sure where else to go. 

I'm here because I've been having some trouble at night. With my eating. It's very embarrassing to admit, and I hope you won't think poorly of me, but... after these nights of eating, I just sit there. I'll have all these crumbs and empty containers just sitting around me, and I feel... oh, I feel so ashamed. Just terribly disgusted with myself. 

I try to be a good person, but it's gotten to the point where I can hardly even bring myself to pray, or... or look the folks at church in the eye the next morning. I know I shouldn't let things get out of hand like that. Is that... does that make sense? Is that the sort of thing you help people with here?
After these episodes of eating, do you ever try to make up for it by making yourself sick, using laxatives, or exercising a lot more than usual?

Oh, goodness, no. I... I would never do anything like that. Making myself sick, or taking those kinds of medicines... that just seems so, well, drastic, doesn't it? I wouldn't want to cause any more trouble for my body than I already have. 

And at my age, my joints aren't really up for heavy exercise anyway. I mostly just... well, like I said, I just sit there and feel awful about what I've done. 

I hope I'm not disappointing you by saying no to that... I know I'm supposed to be taking better care of myself, and I really do want to be good. Is it... is it okay that I haven't been doing those things you mentioned?
Can you tell me what it feels like when you're eating during these episodes? Do you feel like you can't stop eating or control how much you eat once you start?

Oh, goodness... I, um... I hope you won't judge me too harshly for this. That's the hardest part to admit, really. 

It's just that, well... once the house gets quiet at night, and I finally take that first bite of something... it's like my good sense just steps aside. I know I shouldn't be doing it, and even while I'm eating, I'm right there in my head telling myself, 'Belinda, stop now, this isn't right.' But... my hands just keep reaching for more, almost like I can't stop them. 

I feel so foolish admitting that out loud to you. A woman my age ought to have more self-control, shouldn't she? I promise I'm usually very disciplined in other parts of my life, I really try to be good. It sounds terrible, I know... have you ever heard of other people losing their willpower like that? I just want to make sure I'm explaining it right for you, and that I'm giving you the answers you need.
How often do these episodes of eating like this happen to you?

Oh, dear... I really wish I could tell you it was just a rare slip-up. I do try so hard to keep things together, I really do. 

But... well, ever since my dear friend passed away... it seems like these late-night spells have been happening, oh, maybe at least once or twice most weeks. I know that probably sounds like a lot, and I'm so sorry to admit it. I really ought to be doing better than that. 

And... well, if I'm being perfectly honest with you, there hasn't really been a single month where they've let up since she passed. I keep hoping I'll just snap out of it and get back to being my normal, good self. Is... is that terribly often? I hope you don't think I'm just completely hopeless for letting it go on this long.
Do these late-night eating episodes cause you a lot of distress or interfere with your daily life in any way?

Oh, well... I try my best not to let it be a burden to anyone else, I really do. I always want to be helpful and keep a brave face for everyone. But... yes, I suppose it is causing me some trouble. 

I feel so silly even saying it out loud, but... I've actually started making excuses to turn down invitations for my regular bridge nights with the ladies. And... oh, I hate to admit this to you, but I even stepped away from my kitchen duties at the church. 

It's just... well, I get so terribly worried someone might notice the missing leftovers, or... or that they'll just look at my face and ask why I seem so ashamed all the time. I just couldn't bear the thought of them finding out and being disappointed in me. I really do want to get back to being my helpful self, I promise. Does... does that make sense? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of examples for what you need to know.
During these late-night eating episodes, do you find yourself eating much more quickly than usual, almost like you're rushing to finish before you can really think about it?

Oh, my... you really know exactly what to ask, don't you? I... well, I suppose I do. I try to be so polite and proper when I eat with others, I really do. I always take small bites and use my napkin. But when I'm alone in the dark like that... oh, it's so unladylike, I hate to even picture it. 

I'll just be standing right there at the kitchen counter, and... well, I just go so quickly. I eat so fast that I barely even taste the pound cake or the crackers I'm having. Sometimes I... oh, this is so embarrassing... I actually catch myself swallowing before I've even rightly chewed my food. 

It sounds just awful, doesn't it? I know I should sit down at the table and use a proper plate, like a normal person. I really try to have good manners, I promise. Am... am I explaining that clearly enough for your notes? I do hope you don't think too poorly of me for acting so uncivilized in private.
During these late-night eating episodes, do you find yourself eating until you feel uncomfortably full, even if you didn't mean to eat that much?

Oh, dear... well, I always try to stop when I've had a polite amount, I really do. I know a lady shouldn't overindulge. But... yes, I suppose I do keep going a bit too long. 

I feel so dreadful admitting this to you, but... well, I just keep eating until my stomach feels so terribly tight and sore under my nightgown. It gets to the point where I just have to slowly ease myself into the recliner because moving around actually hurts. 

I know I shouldn't let it get that far, and I'm so sorry. I really ought to have better self-control. I promise I'm trying to be better about it. Is... is that the sort of thing you needed to know? I hope my answers are helping you figure this all out.
Do you usually start these late-night eating episodes when you're not actually hungry, maybe even right before bed when you've already had dinner?

Oh, goodness... well, I want to give you the right answer, I really do. But... I'm not entirely sure that fits me. 

I always try to make a nice, sensible dinner for myself in the evening, just like I should. But when I end up back in the kitchen later on... well, I actually do feel quite terribly hungry. My stomach just feels so empty, even if it really shouldn't be. 

I'm so sorry if that's not the normal way this happens, or if it messes up your notes. I just... I really do feel like I'm starving in those moments, like I just haven't eaten a thing all day. I hope I'm not confusing things for you? I'm trying my very best to be helpful.
Do these late-night eating episodes usually happen after something has been bothering you emotionally, like feeling sad, anxious, or stressed?

Oh, my... well, I know it would probably make more sense for your notes if I said yes. I've read about people doing that, you know, eating when they're feeling blue or worked up. But... honestly, I don't think that's it for me. 

I have a very quiet, pleasant life, I really do. I don't have much to be stressed about these days, and I certainly don't want to sound like a complainer making up problems where there aren't any. It seems like these... well, these kitchen visits just happen anyway, even on perfectly lovely days when nothing at all has bothered me. 

I'm so sorry if that's not the answer you were expecting. Is it alright if I say no to that one? I do hope I'm not making your job too difficult by not fitting into the usual pattern... I really am trying to give you the most honest answers I can.
Do you usually eat this way only when you're alone, or do you sometimes eat like this even when others are around?

Oh, heavens no... I would never... well, I mean, I always make sure to be very proper when others are around. I really do try to be good. Like at my bridge club, or the church suppers... I always make a point of just taking a very modest little plate. Just a sensible amount, like a lady should. 

But... oh, this is so embarrassing to say out loud. I hope you won't think terribly of me... but later, after everyone has gone home and the house is completely quiet... that's when I pull the leftovers out. I just stay in the kitchen and eat them all by myself, where nobody can see me. 

I just couldn't bear it if anyone saw me eating like that. I'd die of shame, I really would. Is... is that what you were asking? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right information, I really do want to be helpful.

inference_history.note: The patient reports nighttime eating, shame, and emotional distress around food consumption, which suggests possible eating disorders such as Binge Eating Disorder (F50.81), Night Eating Syndrome (F50.89), or unspecified eating disorder (F50.00). No other conditions have been ruled out yet.

This turn confirmed that the eating episodes cause significant distress and interfere with social functioning (e.g., avoiding social gatherings and stepping away from responsibilities at church), which supports the presence of a disorder. It ruled out F50.89 (Other specified eating disorder) as the presentation more clearly aligns with specific named disorders (Binge Eating Disorder and Night Eating Syndrome, respectively).
